children: Sentinel Holdings' revenue rose 234% year over year, while net loss available to common shareholders widened 38%. Revenue growth reflected the Opsec acquisition and competitive pricing to build its California presence and attract new clients; lower gross profit and higher operating losses contributed to the wider quarterly loss.
¹ Reported as “Revenue”. ² Reported as “Net Income (Loss) Available to Common Shareholders”. ³ Reported as “Net income (loss) including non-controlling interest”.
: Three-month revenue increased 234%, or $1.166M, driven by the Opsec acquisition and the 2026/2027 growth strategy.
: Fell 69%, or $246,000, as the company invested in its growth strategy.
: General and administrative expenses increased $3,000; management cited cost controls and reduced reliance on outside consultants.
: Sentinel sold its USS subsidiary in February 2026 and acquired Opsec client contracts in October 2025.
